note: The format pointer is advanced past '{' and passed to theme_format_expand_abstract, which parses the abstract name and its data.
When the abstract name is followed by a space, data_is_empty is called with p pointing at the space to check if the abstract data is empty.
p is advanced past leading spaces to the first non-space character, which is '$' in the triggering input.
p is incremented past the '$' character, so p now points to the terminating NUL byte of the format string.

code: ret = parse_special((char **) &p, server, active_win == NULL ? NULL : active_win->active, arglist, &free_ret, NULL, 0);
note: parse_special is called with p pointing at '\0'. It immediately returns NULL because **cmd == '\0', without advancing p.
p is incremented again, now pointing one byte past the end of the heap-allocated format string, creating an out-of-bounds pointer.
The loop dereferences p which is now past the end of the heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
